newsitem.title: USA: Green group urges U.S. to help Ogonis in Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: Green group urges U.S. to help Ogonis in Nigeria.

text.p: The Sierra Club Thursday in a letter urged President Clinton to help the Ogoni people of Nigeria "in their struggle against pollution" caused by oil development by Royal Dutch/Shell.

The letter also urged Clinton to press U.S. allies to adopt a series of sanctions against Nigeria on the one-year anniversary of the hanging of nine Nigerian human rights activists including writer Ken Saro-Wiwa after a military appointed tribunal.
Dr. Owens Wiwa, brother of the late writer, signed the letter along with Sierra Club executive director Carl Pope.

"Specifically, we call on you to again press American allies to prohibit new investment in Nigeria, freeze the overseas assets of Nigeria's rulers and, most importantly, impose an oil embargo against the country," the Sierra Club letter said.
Shell operates in Nigeria, but pulled out of Ogoniland in 1993 after the sabotage of its installations by activists in the Movement for the Survival of Ogoni Peoples, which was led by Saro-Wiwa.
The letter said another 19 Ogoni prisoners were being held "on a politically-motivated murder charge for wanting social and environmental justice for the Ogoni people."
"They could also face a military appointed tribunal, an unfair trial and the same hangman's noose unless the Clinton administration and Shell intercede," the letter said.
